issues.translation_quote: I'm plagued by vague suspicions
issues.justification: The Russian is a famous quote with mock-heroic literary flavor, and the translation flattens it. Also a recurring catchphrase, rendered variably ('plagued once more by vague suspicions').

issues.translation_quote: when will this stop?
issues.justification: The source plays on 'кончится' (end) versus Timofeev's 'заканчиваю' (I'm finishing) and the repeated 'когда кончатся ваши опыты'; the English loses the pun-like misunderstanding ('I mean, when will your experiments stop?' does not capture it).

issues.translation_quote: Keep your mouth open!
issues.justification: Mistranslation: the dentist is told not to close his mouth (patient in chair), and the meaning of the line is lost/odd; the English imperative is nonsensical in context.

issues.translation_quote: Let's say she did.
issues.justification: Minor loss, but more importantly 'Ключница' (period-specific keeper of keys) is replaced by 'housekeeper' without humor/period resonance; acceptable but weak.

issues.translation_quote: Score a goal! Score a goal!
issues.justification: The hockey chant 'Шайбу!' (puck) is mistranslated as 'goal'; the anachronistic hockey-fan joke is partly retained but the chant is not rendered faithfully ('Puck!').

issues.source_quote: Вы дo кoтoрoгo часа сегoдня рабoтаете?
issues.translation_quote: What time do you finish work today?
issues.justification: Dropped 'I'll look forward to it'-type addition aside, 'I'll look forward to it' is an invented line added after 'Жду' that changes the speaker's flirtatious tone (acceptable) but 'Жду' meaning 'I'm waiting' is altered.

issues.source_quote: Теряют люди друг друга, а потом не найдут никогда
issues.translation_quote: Finding love is no easy thing
issues.justification: The song's opening line 'С любовью встретиться - проблема трудная' is rendered adequately, but 'Планета вертится, круглая, круглая' loses its childlike rhythm; lyrics lack rhyme and singability.

issues.source_quote: Ты по что боярыню обидел, смерд?!
issues.translation_quote: Why didst thou offend the lady, you peasant?!
issues.justification: Mixes archaic 'didst thou' with modern 'you', producing inconsistent register; the rest of the translation uses no such archaisms.

issues.source_quote: Вы со своими разводами резко снижаете наши показатели.
issues.translation_quote: Your divorces are seriously hurting our statistics.
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the bureaucratic Soviet-speak humor ('показатели' for building's cultural living standards) is not tied to the later 'Model Living Award' joke.

issues.translation_quote: I am most exceedingly... Thank you very much!
issues.justification: The archaic 'Вельми понеже' mixed with modern phrasing is a joke on Bunsha's struggle with period speech; the English drops the contrast and the incomplete phrase is meaningless.

issues.source_quote: Дер гроссер кениг, дас шведишен кенигсрейх, зандте мих.
issues.translation_quote: Der grosser König des schwedischen Königreichs sandte mich, seinen treuen Diener...
issues.justification: The source is deliberately garbled phonetic pseudo-German, and the translation substitutes grammatically polished German with added content ('treuen Diener'), destroying the comic effect and adding material.

issues.source_quote: Был у нас толмач немчин. Ему переводить, а он лыка не вяжет. Мы его в кипятке и сварили.
issues.translation_quote: But he was drunk when we needed him, so we boiled him alive.
issues.justification: 'Лыка не вяжет' means unable to string words together due to drunkenness; acceptable, but the flat rendering loses the colloquial idiom and the deadpan humor.

issues.translation_quote: We'll see to it!
issues.justification: The source line is Bunsha's reply to Georges asking about a jewelry shop; the English omits the shady implication, and 'Does your jewelry shop buy precious stones?' misrepresents who speaks.

issues.translation_quote: The tourist speaks very well!
issues.justification: 'Интурист' is the Soviet agency for foreign tourists, used jokingly for the ambassador; 'The tourist' loses the Soviet cultural reference.

issues.source_quote: Я Вам как представитель общественности заявляю: прекратить!
issues.translation_quote: As a representative of the community, I demand that you stop!
issues.justification: The pompous Soviet 'общественность' bureaucratic flavor is weakened.

issues.source_quote: Три раза я разводилась. Ну да, три. Зюзина я не считаю.
issues.translation_quote: I've been divorced three times. Yes, three. I don't count Zyuzin.
issues.justification: Fine in meaning but 'Please, no scene!' preceding it is an addition that was not in the source and changes the sequence.

issues.translation_quote: Easy, easy! Go ahead.
issues.justification: Speaker attributions are fine, but 'Если ты еще раз вмешаешься... Я тебя...' is rendered with 'I'll...' trailing, losing the threat's directness.

issues.translation_quote: We agree with you completely!
issues.justification: Adequate, but 'Гитлер капут!' and the interpreter jokes rely on timing; OK.

issues.translation_quote: What an odd man you are!
issues.justification: 'Оригинальный' is sarcastic; 'odd' is a bit flat compared with 'quite the character'.

issues.translation_quote: Your Excellency, have mercy.
issues.justification: 'Ваше сиятельство' and 'Ваше благородие' are different titles; the translation inconsistently renders 'Ваше благородие' as 'Your Nobleness', which sounds invented.

issues.source_quote: Ах, боярыня! Красотою лепа, червлена губами, бровьми союзна.
issues.translation_quote: Fair of face, red of lip, with eyebrows joined.
issues.justification: Reasonable, though 'joined eyebrows' is the archaic literary description and may read oddly; acceptable.

issues.translation_quote: I'm no boyar, you fool!
issues.justification: The idiom 'Tambov wolf' is a colorful Soviet insult/saying; the translation neutralizes it.

issues.source_quote: Тоже мне, Тарапунька и Штепсель нашелся.
issues.translation_quote: We've got ourselves a comedy duo.
issues.justification: The cultural reference to the famous Soviet comedy duo is generalized, which is acceptable but loses specificity.

issues.translation_quote: Don't repeat "repeat it"!
issues.justification: The comic confusion in the dictation scene is awkwardly rendered and the earlier lines about 'repeat' become muddled.

issues.source_quote: Блондин - Молчановский. Ну запомни это уже!
issues.translation_quote: Molchanovsky is the blond one. Do try to remember!
issues.justification: Fine; but 'Is he the tall blond one?' preceding it omits 'как его' hesitation.
